profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a U.S. law review between the lead author of a forthcoming symposium article, 'When Europe Hits Home: Europeanization and Domestic Change,' and the journal's managing editor. The article has been accepted subject to editorial revisions for a special issue on comparative public law. They are syncing on handoffs between the author team and the journal: which post-revision file will anchor the next exchange, what the Friday source delivery should include, what 'locking the manuscript' means for scheduling cite-check, and how EU legal authorities will be 'standardized' before production. The agenda is to align on interfaces between author revisions and student-editor workflows, confirm who will supply which materials, and keep the symposium production calendar on track. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the Friday handoff package, the basis for cite-check assignments, and the treatment of EU citations, even though subtle differences remain about the content and scope of each deliverable.

members.name: Dr. Elena Varga
members.role: Associate Professor of EU Law and lead author
members.expertise: European integration, comparative constitutional law, and socio-legal institutional analysis
members.background: Elena teaches EU governance at a Dutch university and regularly publishes in European public law journals, where authors often continue polishing footnotes and citation presentation after the substantive draft is considered settled.
members.private_state: She wants to preserve doctrinal nuance in the article's treatment of EU and member-state materials while minimizing time spent reworking citations into unfamiliar U.S. conventions, and she is wary of student editors flattening distinctions that matter to European lawyers.
hidden_assumptions: When someone refers to 'the post-revision file from Tuesday,' they mean the clean author-controlled manuscript she sent after integrating co-author comments, because that is the real substantive baseline.

A 'sources package' means a selective set of hard-to-obtain or non-English materials, since standard EU treaties, directives, and major Court of Justice decisions are publicly accessible and need not be duplicated.
'Locking the manuscript' means the argument structure, section order, and cited authorities are fixed, even if some pinpoints, parentheticals, and translation notes may still be refined.

'Standardizing the EU citations' means making the article internally consistent using accepted European legal identifiers and references, such as stable ECLI citations, official case names, and uniform EUR-Lex references, not replacing them wholesale with U.S.-style formatting.

members.name: Marcus Lee
members.role: Managing Editor, law review symposium issue
members.expertise: Editorial workflow coordination, source collection, and cite-check logistics for public law scholarship
members.background: Marcus is a third-year U.S. law student overseeing editorial operations for the symposium issue and is used to law review processes where a board-controlled master file, complete source set, and stable footnote layout are prerequisites for efficient cite-check assignment.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid re-batching assignments or leaving student editors to improvise on foreign and EU authorities, and he is trying to keep the production schedule stable without signaling uncertainty about non-U.S. legal materials.
hidden_assumptions: When someone refers to 'the post-revision file from Tuesday,' they mean the Tuesday journal file incorporating house-style edits and tracked changes, because the operational version is the one the board can assign from.

A 'sources package' means a comprehensive set of materials for every citation in the manuscript, including standard EU authorities, PDFs, links, screenshots, and translations where relevant, so no editor has to hunt for anything independently.
'Locking the manuscript' means the footnotes are frozen in number, order, and pin-cite detail, because cite-check batching and source logs depend on a stable note structure.

'Standardizing the EU citations' means conforming all EU and foreign authorities to the journal's Bluebook-based house style so the final piece reads consistently within the law review's citation system.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Tuesday post-revision file anchors the handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to use 'the post-revision file from Tuesday' for the Friday handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the clean manuscript she emailed Tuesday morning after folding in co-author revisions and finalizing the substantive text.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the journal's Tuesday afternoon master document with house-style edits and tracked changes, which he regards as the assignable version for editors.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both sides really did exchange a meaningful Tuesday file after revisions, so the phrase sounds unusually specific and therefore safe; each assumes there is only one obvious 'post-revision' Tuesday version worth discussing.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on Elena sending 'the sources package' with the Friday materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this includes only difficult-to-access items such as German-language scholarship, constitutional court decisions in local databases, and policy reports not easily retrievable by a U.S. student editor.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this includes every authority cited in the article, including EUR-Lex copies of directives, treaty materials, Court of Justice cases, book excerpts, and any needed translation support.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In both of their professional contexts, 'sources package' is routine shorthand that usually does not require redefinition; each experiences their own scope as the obvious default and hears the other's agreement as confirmation.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to lock the manuscript
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the article will be 'locked' by Friday so cite-check can begin.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes 'locked' to mean the article's argument, structure, and source list are settled, while minor footnote polishing such as pinpoints, short forms, and translation parentheticals can continue without changing the manuscript in any meaningful sense.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes 'locked' to mean the footnote apparatus is frozen enough for assignment sheets and source logs to remain stable, including pin cites and note ordering.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a normal milestone rather than a negotiable threshold, and both are genuinely describing the moment after major revisions are done; the disagreement sits in the quiet operational standard for what still counts as 'minor' movement.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the EU materials should be 'standardized' before production.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means harmonizing the EU citations internally by using consistent European conventions such as official case names, ECLI identifiers, and uniform references to treaties and EUR-Lex materials.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means converting the EU and foreign citations into the journal's Bluebook-oriented house style, even where that changes ordering, abbreviations, or which identifiers are foregrounded.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are discussing consistency in citation presentation, so 'standardized' sounds like straightforward housekeeping rather than a site of substantive difference; neither expects the other to hear the term as pointing to a different citation authority.
